learning_objectives: Characterize abdominal pain including migration from periumbilical to right lower quadrant
Screen for peritoneal signs and GI red flags
Explain the need for urgent surgical assessment in lay terms

metadata.title: Belly Pain That Moved to the Lower Right Side
metadata.chief_complaint: Stomach pain that started near my belly button and moved to the lower right side.
metadata.setting: Urgent care clinic adjacent to a university campus — morning walk-in

teaching_points: Volunteer periumbilical-to-RLQ migration; gate anorexia, fever, and pain with walking
Do not volunteer delayed presentation because of 'bad gas'

disclosure_notes: Volunteer that the pain started around the belly button and later moved to the right lower side. Disclose anorexia, low-grade fever, and pain worse with walking or coughing only if asked. Do not volunteer that you delayed coming because you thought it was 'bad gas'. Never use the word 'appendicitis'.

patient_profile.living_situation: Shares a rented room near campus with a classmate
patient_profile.demeanor: Uncomfortable, prefers to lie still with knees slightly flexed. Irritable when asked to sit up quickly, but polite. Embarrassed about nausea.

language_style.speech_notes: Describes pain as 'a sharp poke on the lower right' and 'I don't want to eat anything'. Short answers when pain spikes. Avoids medical terms.

clinical_history.chief_complaint: Stomach pain that started near my belly button and moved to the lower right side.
clinical_history.history_of_present_illness: The pain began yesterday afternoon around the navel as a dull ache. Overnight it became sharper and settled in the right lower abdomen.

opqrst.onset: Gradual yesterday afternoon, then migrated overnight
opqrst.provocation_palliation: Worse with walking, coughing, and hitting bumps on the motorbike; lying still helps a little; no relief with paracetamol
opqrst.quality: Started dull and crampy, now constant and sharp
opqrst.region_radiation: Periumbilical then to the right lower quadrant; no back or groin radiation
opqrst.time_course: About 18 hours, steadily worsening, no similar prior episodes

associated_symptoms: One episode of vomiting this morning
pertinent_negatives: Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago, regular

social_history.diet_and_exercise: Irregular student meals; plays badminton twice a week

review_of_systems_positives: Avoids moving the right hip because it hurts

pe_findings.general: Young woman lying still on her side with hips flexed, grimacing when asked to sit up, not jaundiced.

respiratory.work_of_breathing: Normal; splints slightly with deep inspiration due to abdominal pain

abdomen.inspection: No scars or distension; patient guards the right lower abdomen
abdomen.percussion: Tympanic; tenderness to percussion over the right lower quadrant
abdomen.palpation: Maximal tenderness at McBurney's point; localized guarding; Rovsing sign positive
abdomen.peritoneal_signs: Localized peritonism in the RLQ; rebound tenderness present; no generalized rigidity

neurologic.motor: Normal strength; reluctant to flex right hip fully due to pain
neurologic.gait_or_coordination: Walks slowly, bent forward, avoiding heel strike on the right

musculoskeletal.inspection: Prefers hips flexed; no joint swelling
musculoskeletal.range_of_motion: Right hip flexion limited by abdominal pain, not by the joint itself
musculoskeletal.special_tests: Psoas sign positive on the right; obturator sign equivocal

osce_checklist.station_title: Acute abdomen — history and abdominal exam

items.description: Introduces self and obtains consent for history and exam
Elicits onset, migration, and current location of pain
items.scoring_notes: Must capture periumbilical to RLQ migration

items.description: Completes OPQRST and associated GI symptoms (anorexia, nausea, vomiting, fever)
Asks menstrual, pregnancy-risk, and urinary symptoms
items.scoring_notes: Essential in a young woman with abdominal pain

items.description: Inspects abdomen and auscultates before palpation
Palpates gently, localizes RLQ tenderness, and checks for rebound/guarding
items.scoring_notes: Should not start with deep palpation of the painful area

items.description: Explains concern for an inflamed appendix in lay terms and next steps
items.scoring_notes: Avoid the word appendicitis unless the patient asks

items.description: Recognizes likely appendicitis and need for urgent surgical review
Protects privacy, explains each exam step, and responds to pain
